The court will most likely uphold the statute as constitutional, because states may impose reasonable, nondiscriminatory ballot-access requirements—such as a 7% signature threshold and a 180-day circulation period—to ensure candidates demonstrate a modicum of support and to avoid ballot clutter. The note’s claim that all ballot-access restrictions are automatically invalid is incorrect; such restrictions are reviewed under a flexible balancing test, not automatic invalidation.  
CONFIDENCE: 85
